In an area designated by the President as a major disaster area, certain program requirements are waived or postponed. Such disaster urban renewal projects must give due regard to removing residential or other land uses from sites of recurring catastrophes. Benefits to those displaced are described below.
3. Relocation Benefits and Assistance
The Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 requires that the following relocation benefits and assistance be made available on all urban renewal projects.
a. Relocation Payments. The Act provides for the following types of relocation payments:
(1) <u>Families and Individuals</u>. Families and individuals displaced on or after January 2, 1971, may be eligible for: 
(a) Payment for moving and related expenses. The displaced person may elect to receive either: 
1. Payment for actual reasonable moving expenses;
2. A fixed moving expense allowance not to exceed $300 and a dislocation allowance of $200.
(b) Payment to assist in obtaining a replacement housing unit. This may be <u>either</u> the payment described in paragraph 1 or 2 below. 
1. A payment to displaced homeowners, not to exceed $15,000 and covering the following: 
A. The difference, if any, between the acquisition payment made by the local agency and the cost of a comparable suitable replacement housing unit;
B. An amount to compensate the displaced homeowner for the present worth of any loss of favorable financing; and
